decisions.reason: This is essentially an evolution of an already accepted trommel screen, so it builds directly on the firm's existing screening know-how and early customer recognition.
The mobile high-speed flail shredders fit the firm's core mobile waste-processing capabilities and service network, making them a related line the firm is well placed to refine commercially.
A mobile high-speed grinder is close to the firm's established knowledge base in mobile recycling machinery, although the limited market evidence visible so far leaves some uncertainty.

The stationary electric fine shredder matches the firm's stationary processing expertise and its strategic push toward resource-saving solutions, so management would likely continue learning and improving rather than exit quickly.

The green-waste grinder is still related to the firm's grinder portfolio and customer base, but its narrower application and overlap with other grinder models make it somewhat more vulnerable if demand is weaker than expected.

Stationary single-shaft pre-shredders are strongly aligned with the firm's existing shredding competences and were given a clear market presentation, indicating a high willingness to keep and develop the line.
